## Question 4 - Logistic Regression

# Load related Libraries/Functions/Variables

Functions files are from Section 08 folder

```{r Setup}
library(MASS)
library(class)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)

load("cancer_PC.RData")
load("BCWData_balanced.RData")

sapply(list.files(as.character(here("functions")),
                  pattern = "*.R",
                  full.names = TRUE,
                  ignore.case = TRUE),
       source,
       .GlobalEnv)
```

# Select Principal Components for 90% Variance

```{r PC_select, echo=FALSE}
cancer_pc_summary <- summary(cancer_PC)
cumulative_var <- cancer_pc_summary$importance[3, ]
num_PCs <- which(cumulative_var >= 0.90)[1]

cat("Number of PCs needed for 90% variance:", num_PCs, "\n")
```

Store into a dataset

```{r update data, echo=FALSE}
BCWData_pca_90perVar <- as.data.frame(predict(cancer_PC,BCWData_balanced)[, 1:num_PCs])

```

# Convert Class labels

2 = Benign -\> 0, 4 = Malignant -\> 1

```{r Class convert, echo=FALSE}
BCWData_pca_90perVar$Class <- ifelse(BCWData_balanced$Class == "2", 0, 1)

str(BCWData_pca_90perVar)
```

# Split Data to Training & Testing sets

Define `%w/o%` in "get.train().R". And the define function is from "without.R" in Section 8 folder.

```{r helper Define, echo=FALSE }
"%w/o%" <- function(x,y) x[!x %in% y]
```

In machine learning, a common split for a dataset is 80% for training and 20% for testing. In other words, the split_indices is adjustable.

```{r TrainTest Sets, echo=FALSE}
set.seed(123)  

split_indices <- get.train(nrow(BCWData_pca_90perVar), train.sz = round(0.8 * nrow(BCWData_pca_90perVar)))

train_data <- BCWData_pca_90perVar[split_indices$train, ] 
test_data <- BCWData_pca_90perVar[split_indices$test, ]   

train_data$Class <- as.factor(train_data$Class)
test_data$Class <- as.factor(test_data$Class)

cat("Training samples:", nrow(train_data), "\n")
cat("Test samples:", nrow(test_data), "\n")
```

# Logistic Regression Model

```{r LR Model, echo=FALSE}
log_model <- glm(Class ~ ., data = train_data, family = binomial(link = "logit"))

summary(log_model)
```

# Visualizing Logistic Regression

Name the PC for the visualization
```{r Axis_name, echo=FALSE}
pc_name_mapping <- c(
    "PC1" = "Uniformity of Cell Size",
    "PC2" = "Mitoses",
    "PC3" = "Clump Thickness",
    "PC4" = "Bare Nuclei",
    "PC5" = "Normal Nucleoli",
    "PC6" = "Marginal Adhesion",
    "PC7" = "Bland Chromatin"
)
```

Visualize the first 2 PCs (PC 1 vs PC 2)
```{r Visualization_initial, echo=FALSE}
model.exp <- expression(glm(Class ~ ., data = train_data, family = binomial(link = "logit")))
predict.exp <- expression((p.hat(model, points) > 0.5) * 1)

train_data_renamed <- train_data
colnames(train_data_renamed)[1:2] <- c("Mitoses", "Uniformity of Cell Size")

example.display(train_data_renamed, train_data$Class, {}, {},
                c(100, 100), "Logistic Regression ( Clump Thickness vs Uniformity of Cell Size )",
                model.exp, predict.exp)
```

Since the graph doesn't show much difference. Find the best 2 PCs for Visualization (highest coeff)

```{r Visualization_SetUp, echo=FALSE}
coef_values <- abs(coef(log_model)[-1])  
best_pcs <- names(sort(coef_values, decreasing = TRUE))[1:2]  

best_pcs_named <- pc_name_mapping[best_pcs]

train_pca_2D <- train_data[, c(best_pcs, "Class")]
colnames(train_pca_2D)[1:2] <- best_pcs_named
train_pca_2D$Class <- as.factor(train_pca_2D$Class)
train_pca_2D_matrix <- as.matrix(train_pca_2D[, 1:2])
```

Visualize using `example.display()`

```{r Visualization_p1, echo=FALSE}
model.exp <- expression(glm(Class ~ ., data = train_pca_2D, family = binomial(link = "logit")))
predict.exp <- expression((p.hat(model, points) > 0.5) * 1)

example.display(train_pca_2D_matrix, train_pca_2D$Class, {}, {},
                c(100, 100), paste("Logistic Regression (", best_pcs_named[1], " vs ", best_pcs_named[2], ")"),
                model.exp, predict.exp)
```

## Question 5 - Confusion Matrix

(Predict vs Actual values)

```{r Confusion Matrix, echo=FALSE}
library(mda)

pred_probs <- predict(log_model, test_data, type = "response")
predictions <- ifelse(pred_probs > 0.5, 1, 0) 

predictions <- as.factor(predictions)
test_class <- test_data$Class

confusion_matrix <- mda::confusion(predictions, test_class)
confusion_matrix_expanded <- confusion.expand(predictions, test_class)

print(confusion_matrix)
print(confusion_matrix_expanded)
```

## Question 6 - Classification Quality

Extract value from the confusion matrix

```{r Extract value, echo=FALSE}
TP <- confusion_matrix[2, 2]
TN <- confusion_matrix[1, 1]
FP <- confusion_matrix[2, 1]
FN <- confusion_matrix[1, 2]

cat("True positive :", TP, "\n")
cat("True negative :", TN, "\n")
cat("False positive :", FP, "\n")
cat("False negative :", FN, "\n")
```

Calculate the performances

```{r Performance Calculation, echo=FALSE}
accuracy <- (TP + TN) / (TP + FP + FN + TN)
recall <- TP / (TP + FN)
specificity <- TN / (FP + TN)
precision <- TP / (TP + FP)
f1_score <- (2 * TP) / (2 * TP + FP + FN)
```

Calculate the AUC Reference: <https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/plotting-roc-curve-in-r-programming/>

```{r AUC Calculation, echo=FALSE}
library(pROC)

roc_curve <- roc(test_class, pred_probs)
plot(roc_curve, col = "blue", main = "ROC Curve", print.auc = TRUE)
abline(a = 0, b = 1, lty = 2, col = "red")

auc <- as.numeric(roc_curve$auc)
```

Display Performance Result

```{r Performance Output}
cat("Logistic Regression Model Performance Metrics\n")
cat("---------------------------\n")
cat("Accuracy:", round(accuracy, 4), "\n")
cat("Recall:", round(recall, 4), "\n")
cat("Specificity:", round(specificity, 4), "\n")
cat("Precision:", round(precision, 4), "\n")
cat("F1 Score:", round(f1_score, 4), "\n")
cat("AUC:", round(auc, 4), "\n")
```
